issues.t: Harsh or clunky automatic shifts
issues.sym: A thump or metallic clunk when the automatic changes gear, rough downshifts, and now and then a delay before it engages, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: Shift control on these automatics can produce firm, poorly timed shifts. Dodge released updated transmission control software for the complaint.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check for stored codes and transmission software updates, and have the fluid level checked.

issues.t: Front wheel spindle nut may loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or looseness from a front wheel, a wobble, or in the worst case the wheel coming away from the car.
issues.why: The nut holding the front wheel hub to the spindle may not have been tightened correctly, so the wheel and tire could separate while driving.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. If a front wheel clunks or feels loose, stop driving and have it towed in.

issues.t: Key can come out before the car is in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The key fob can be pulled from the ignition while the shifter is not in Park.
issues.why: A fault in the wireless ignition node module let the key be removed out of Park, so the car could roll away after the driver leaves.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. Until it is fixed, always confirm the car is in Park and set the parking brake before getting out.

issues.t: Power steering hose can leak and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leaking in the engine bay, a burning smell, smoke from under the hood, or a whining pump from low fluid.
issues.why: The crimped end of the power steering pressure hose can separate. Fluid that sprays onto hot engine parts could catch fire.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. If you see smoke or smell burning fluid, pull over, shut the engine off and do not drive until it is repaired.

issues.t: Alternator can fail suddenly (recall)
issues.sym: Battery light or several warning lights at once, dimming electrics, a burning smell, then stalling or a no-start. Some owners reported smoke.
issues.why: The 160-amp alternator on the V6 could fail internally without warning, cutting power and stalling the engine. Chrysler recalled it and later expanded the campaign.
issues.next: Check the VIN for both recalls. If the battery light comes on, get off the road safely; the car may stall soon.

issues.t: Left cylinder head failure
issues.sym: Ticking from the driver's side of the engine, misfire, rough running, a flashing or steady check engine light, and sometimes stalling.
issues.why: Early versions of the left cylinder head could crack. Chrysler extended the warranty on the left head and changed the design in late 2012.
issues.next: If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Ask a dealer whether the extended head coverage still applies.

issues.t: Power distribution module (TIPM) failure
issues.sym: Engine cranks but will not start or does not crank at all, the horn or wipers act on their own, power windows stop working, or random electrical faults.
issues.why: The Totally Integrated Power Module, which routes power to many circuits, can develop internal faults.
issues.next: Have the module diagnosed before replacing other parts like the starter or fuel pump. Check for any recalls or service programs that apply.

issues.t: Cruise control may not turn off (recall)
issues.sym: Cruise control stays on when you press the brake or the cancel button, and the car may hold speed or speed up.
issues.why: A wiring short while cruise control is on could stop the system from switching off. Chrysler recalled the cars for a software update.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and avoid using cruise control until it is done. If it will not cancel, brake firmly, shift to Neutral and stop safely.

issues.t: HEMI tick from failed lifters and worn camshaft
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping from the engine that is loudest after a cold start and rises with engine speed, sometimes with a misfire or check engine light.
issues.why: The small rollers on the valve lifters can stop turning and flatten, then grind into the camshaft lobes. Owners and shops report it on these HEMI engines, often at higher mileage and sometimes sooner.
issues.next: Have a new tick diagnosed soon. A failed lifter keeps chewing up the camshaft and spreads metal through the oil, so catching it early can save the engine. If there is a flashing check engine light, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Broken exhaust manifold bolts
issues.sym: A ticking or puffing sound near the back of the engine, loudest when cold and fading as it warms up, sometimes with an exhaust smell.
issues.why: The cast iron manifolds get very hot at the rear and can warp, which snaps the bolts holding them to the cylinder heads, most often the rear bolt on the passenger side. The gap lets exhaust leak out.
issues.next: Have a mechanic check the manifold bolts before assuming the lifters are bad, since the two sounds are easy to confuse. If the manifold is warped, replacing only the bolts usually does not last.

issues.t: Oil filter housing and oil cooler leak
issues.sym: Oil (and sometimes coolant) collecting in the valley on top of the engine or dripping at the back of the engine, a burning oil smell, and the oil level dropping between changes.
issues.why: The plastic oil filter housing, which also holds the oil cooler, sits between the cylinder banks where it gets very hot. Over time the plastic can warp or crack and its seals harden and leak.
issues.next: Check the oil level often and have the housing inspected if you see oil on top of the engine. Do not let the oil run low; if coolant is also being lost, watch the temperature gauge and get it fixed promptly.

issues.t: Rear differential whine or failure
issues.sym: A whine or howl from the rear of the car, usually between about 45 and 65 mph, a vibration from the back, or clunks when accelerating. In bad cases the car loses drive to the rear wheels.
issues.why: Owners of V8 models, especially the high-powered versions, report worn gears and bearings inside the rear differential. A class-action lawsuit claims the differentials can fail outright.
issues.next: Have a new rear-end whine checked soon and the differential fluid inspected. If there are loud clunks or grinding, or the car stops pulling, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Engine can be shut off out of Park with Keyless Go (recall)
issues.sym: On cars with the Keyless Go option, the engine can be switched off while the shifter is not in Park.
issues.why: The ignition module did not stop the engine from being turned off unless the transmission was in Park, so the car could be left in gear and roll away. Chrysler reprogrammed the module.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. Until it is done, always put the car in Park and set the parking brake before switching off and getting out.

issues.t: Takata airbag inflator can rupture (do-not-drive recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning at all. The danger only shows in a crash, when the airbag inflator can burst and throw metal pieces into the cabin.
issues.why: The airbag propellant breaks down over years of heat and humidity. The driver airbag on 2008-2010 cars and the passenger airbag on 2008-2014 cars were recalled, and these campaigns carry a do-not-drive warning.
issues.next: Check the VIN right away. If an airbag recall is open, do not drive the car; ask the dealer to tow it or come to you for the free replacement.

issues.t: Tire pressure sensors may not report real pressure (recall)
issues.sym: The tire pressure warning light stays off even though a tire is low, or the readings do not match the tires.
issues.why: Some tire pressure sensors could fail to report actual pressure, so the system would not warn about an underinflated tire. Chrysler replaced the sensors.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and check tire pressures with a gauge until the sensors are replaced.

issues.t: Seat side airbags may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag warning light may come on, though often there is no sign until a crash.
issues.why: Crimped connections in the seat side-airbag wiring were undersized, so the side airbags might not work when needed. Chrysler replaced the harnesses.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and have it done promptly. Do not ignore an airbag warning light.

issues.t: Battery cable at the starter can short and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from low on the engine, flickering electrics, or a no-start.
issues.why: The battery cable running to the starter could rub through and short to ground, which can overheat and start a fire. This campaign carried a do-not-drive warning until repaired.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. If it is open, do not drive the car until the cable is replaced. If you see smoke, pull over and shut the engine off.

issues.t: Fuel rail crossover hose can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A strong fuel smell around the engine, or fuel dripping or wetness on the engine.
issues.why: On SRT models the hose that links the two fuel rails could leak, putting fuel near hot engine parts and creating a fire risk. Chrysler replaced the hose.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, stop driving and shut the engine off. Check the VIN for this recall and have it fixed before driving again.

issues.t: Instrument cluster may go blank (recall)
issues.sym: The gauges and warning lights stop working while driving.
issues.why: A software fault could shut down the instrument cluster, so the driver loses speed readings and warnings. Chrysler updated the software.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and have the software update done.

issues.t: Radio software could allow remote hacking (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms in normal driving.
issues.why: A flaw in the Uconnect radio software could let someone access vehicle systems remotely through the cellular connection. Chrysler issued a software update.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and make sure the radio update was installed.

issues.t: Side curtain airbag mounting bolt loose or missing (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning; sometimes a rattle from the roof edge.
issues.why: A bolt that holds the side curtain airbag could be loose or missing, so the airbag might not deploy properly in a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and have the airbag mounting inspected promptly.

issues.t: Engine oil cooler hoses can fail (recall)
issues.sym: Oil spraying or dripping under the hood, smoke, a burning smell, or an oil pressure warning.
issues.why: The hoses feeding the engine oil cooler on Hellcat models could fail and spray oil, which risks engine damage and fire. Chrysler replaced the lines.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. If you see oil spraying or smoke, stop and shut the engine off right away.

issues.t: Car may not stay in Park (recalls)
issues.sym: The car rolls after being put in Park, or Park does not fully engage.
issues.why: On some 2017 cars a software issue meant Park might not be reliably engaged when the driver got out; some 2018 cars had an incorrect park lock rod fitted in the transmission. Both were recalled.
issues.next: Check the VIN for these recalls. Always set the parking brake before leaving the car until the repair is done.

issues.t: Engine computer can fail and stall the car (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving or will not start.
issues.why: A chip in the powertrain control module could fail, shutting the engine down. Chrysler replaced the module.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. If the car stalls, get off the road safely and have it towed for the repair.

issues.t: Wrong wheel and brake combination can rub the tire (recall)
issues.sym: Scraping or rubbing from a front wheel, especially when turning, and visible damage on the tire.
issues.why: Some cars were built with a front wheel and brake package that did not match, so parts could contact and damage the tire. Chrysler replaced the wheels and checked tires and alignment.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. If you hear rubbing from a front wheel, stop driving and have it inspected before the tire fails.

issues.t: Instrument cluster may not show warnings (recall)
issues.sym: Warning messages and lights that should appear on the dash do not show up.
issues.why: A software fault could stop the instrument cluster from displaying some driver warnings. Chrysler updated the cluster software.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and have the update installed.

issues.t: Backup camera image may stay on (recall)
issues.sym: The rear camera picture stays on the screen after you shift out of Reverse.
issues.why: A radio software error could leave the camera view displayed, which hides other information and does not meet the federal standard. It was fixed by a software update.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall; the update can be installed by a dealer or over the air.

issues.t: Windshield may not be properly bonded (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning; in some cases wind noise or a windshield that seems loose at the edges.
issues.why: The urethane that bonds the windshield may not have been applied correctly, so the glass might not stay in place in a crash. Dealers reapply the sealant.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and get it repaired soon.

issues.t: Safety warning lights may be too dim to see (recall)
issues.sym: Dash warning lights for safety systems are hard or impossible to see.
issues.why: The instrument cluster could show some safety indicators too faintly. Chrysler reprogrammed the cluster.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and have the cluster reprogrammed.

issues.t: Tire pressure sensor batteries can die early (recall)
issues.sym: A tire pressure warning or system fault light, or missing pressure readings for one or more tires.
issues.why: The batteries inside the tire pressure sensors could run down early, so the system stops warning about low tires. The recall was later expanded to more cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for both campaigns and check tire pressures with a gauge until the sensors are replaced.

issues.t: Parking brake may be misadjusted (recall)
issues.sym: The parking brake does not hold the car well on a slope, or the lever feels too loose.
issues.why: The parking brake may have been set up incorrectly at the factory, so it might not hold the car and it could roll away. Dealers readjust it.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. Until it is done, park on level ground and make sure the car is in Park.

issues.t: Left rear seatback may not lock upright (recall)
issues.sym: The left rear seatback does not latch or can be pushed forward.
issues.why: The latch striker may be out of position, so the seatback might not lock and could fold forward in a crash. Dealers adjust the striker.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and avoid seating passengers behind an unlatched seatback.
